questions.q: What question does a Percent of Total table calculation answer?
options: What share of a whole does each value represent?
How much did this value change from the last one?
What is the rank of this value compared to others?
What is the running sum of all values so far?
questions.explain: Percent of Total expresses each value as a percentage share of a total — which total depends entirely on the Compute Using setting.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, why does January show as 19.11% under one Compute Using setting?
options: Because Compute Using was set to Pane (down), scoping the 'total' to just that quarter
Because 19.11% is a fixed value that never changes regardless of settings
Because January always represents a fixed percentage of any total in Tableau
Percent of Total ignores the Compute Using setting entirely
questions.explain: Percent of Total is only meaningful once you know what it's a percent of — Compute Using: Pane (down) scoped the calculation to each quarter, so January's percentage is relative to that quarter's total, not the whole table.

questions.q: What does Percent Difference show, versus plain Difference?
options: Difference shows the raw gap between two values; Percent Difference expresses that same gap as a percentage of the reference value
They are identical calculations with two different names
Percent Difference only works on dates, never on measures
Difference can only compare to the first value in the view, never the previous one
questions.explain: Difference gives the raw numeric gap (e.g., in dollars); Percent Difference gives that same gap as a percentage of the earlier ('Relative to') value.

questions.q: What does the LOOKUP(expression, -1) function do in the underlying table calc formula for Difference?
options: It reaches back one position in the view to get the previous value to compare against
It filters out negative numbers from the view
It looks up a value from a completely different data source
It converts the expression to a percentage
questions.explain: LOOKUP(expression, offset) reaches to a different row relative to the current one — an offset of -1 is what 'Relative to Previous' means underneath the Percent Difference dialog.

questions.q: Why is the very first value in a 'Percent Difference from Previous' column always blank?
options: There is no previous row for the first value to compare against
Tableau always hides the first row of any table calculation
The first row's data is always zero in Sample Superstore
Percent Difference requires at least three rows of data before it will calculate anything
questions.explain: Since Percent Difference From compares each value to the one before it (by default), the first row in the partition has nothing prior to reference, so its calculated value is blank.
